back_translation: The LORD has declared: "Woe to the rebellious children, who carry out a plan that is not Mine, who make a treaty not born of My Spirit, heaping up sin upon sin.
They set out to go down to Egypt without asking from My mouth, to seek shelter in Pharaoh's stronghold and to take refuge in the shade of Egypt.
But Pharaoh's stronghold will become your shame, and refuge in Egypt's shade your disgrace.
For though his princes are at Zoan and his envoys have reached Hanes,
everyone will be put to shame because of a people useless to them, who bring neither help nor profit, but only shame and disgrace."

The burden concerning the beasts of the Negev: Through a land of hardship and anguish, a land of the lioness and roaring lion, of the viper and the flying burning serpent, they carry their wealth on the backs of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people of no profit.
As for Egypt, its help is futile and empty; therefore I have called her "Rahab Who Sits Idle."
Now go, write this on a tablet before them and record it in a scroll, so that for the days to come it will be a witness forever and ever.
For these are a defiant people, lying children, children unwilling to hear the instruction of the LORD,
who say to the seers, "See no visions!" and to the prophets, "Do not prophesy the truth to us. Speak pleasant things to us; prophesy deceptive illusions.
Get out of this way; turn aside from this path. Take the Holy One of Israel out of our presence!"
Therefore the Holy One of Israel says this: "Because you have rejected this word and trusted in oppression and relied on deceit,
therefore this iniquity will be to you like a crack about to fall, like a bulge in a high wall whose collapse comes suddenly, in the blink of an eye.
It will break like a potter's vessel smashed to pieces without mercy, so that among its shattered fragments not a shard can be found to scoop coals from a hearth or to dip water from a cistern."
For the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, has said: "In returning and rest you will be saved; in quietness and trust will be your strength" — but you were not willing.
Instead you said, "No, we will flee on horses" — therefore you will indeed flee! And, "We will ride swift horses" — therefore your pursuers will be swifter!
A thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you will all flee, until you are left like a mast on a mountaintop, like a signal banner on a hill.
Therefore the LORD waits to be gracious to you; therefore He will rise up to show you mercy. For the LORD is a God of justice; blessed are all who wait for Him!
O people in Zion who dwell in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you when the sound of your cry for help goes up; when He hears, He will answer you.
Though the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, your Teacher will no longer hide Himself; your eyes will see your Teacher.
And whenever you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear a word from behind you, saying, "This is the way; walk in it."
Then you will defile your silver-plated carved idols and your gold-plated cast images. You will throw them away like a woman's menstrual cloth and say to them, "Be gone!"
Then He will give rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and the food that is the produce of the land will be rich and abundant. In that day your livestock will graze in broad pastures.
The oxen and donkeys that work the ground will eat seasoned fodder, winnowed with shovel and fork.
And on every high mountain and every lofty hill there will be streams and flowing watercourses, in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter — like the light of seven days combined — in the day the LORD binds up the brokenness of His people and heals the wound He inflicted.
Behold, the Name of the LORD comes from afar. His anger burns, and the smoke is thick. His lips are full of indignation, and His tongue is like a consuming fire.
His breath is like an overflowing torrent rising up to the neck, to sift the nations in a sieve of destruction, and to place on the jaws of the peoples a bridle that leads them astray.
But you will have a song, as on the night of a holy festival, and your heart will rejoice like one walking to the sound of a flute, going up to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
And the LORD will cause His majestic voice to be heard and will reveal His arm descending in fierce anger and a flame of consuming fire, with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.
For Assyria will be shattered with terror at the voice of the LORD; He will strike them with His scepter.
And every stroke of the rod of punishment that the LORD brings down upon them will be to the sound of tambourines and lyres; He will fight against them with His hand raised in battle.

For Topheth has long been prepared; it has been made ready for that king. Its fire-pit is deep and wide, with fire and wood in abundance. The breath of the LORD, like a stream of burning sulfur, will set it ablaze.
